info.name: Zameens — Full API (merged)
info.description: Merged from Zameens-Admin, Zameens-Commerce-Payments, Zameens-Dev1, Zameens-Dev2 and Zameens-Organizations into a single collection, deduplicated by module. Auth defaults to {{accessToken}}; everything under Admin defaults to {{adminAccessToken}} via a folder-level auth override.

item.name: Request OTP (Member — email)
item.description: Run Members / Add member (invite by email) first — this logs in as the account that invite just created (or reused) for {{memberEmail}}.

item.name: Verify OTP (Member) → sets memberAccessToken
item.description: OTP is logged to the server console in non-production — set the {{otp}} collection variable from there before running this.

item.name: Create media upload tickets (batch)
item.description: Selecting multiple files at once: pass a `files` array (up to 20) instead of a single file object. The response returns `{ "files": [...] }` with one upload ticket per file, in the same order.

item.name: Complete media upload (batch)
item.description: Each entry needs the storageKey returned by its own upload ticket. All files are saved atomically in one request; the response returns `{ "files": [...] }` with the created media records.

{
  "transactionType": "SALE",
  "title": "Land parcel for sale in Panvel",

  "priceAmountMinor": 100000000,

item.name: Feature listing (plan allowance, falls back to paid checkout)
item.description:
No request body. Draws one unit from the listing owner's plan-included monthly featuredListingsPerMonth allowance and grants the promotion immediately — no checkout, no payment. On success: `{ "listingId", "promotionType": "FEATURED", "endsAt" }`.

- 409 LISTING_ALREADY_FEATURED if the listing already has an active FEATURED promotion (from either this endpoint or a paid purchase) — nothing is consumed.
- 403 PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED (`error.details.feature: "FEATURED_LISTINGS", upgradeRequired: true, checkoutRequired: true`) if the owner's plan has no allowance left this month (or none at all) — fall back to the paid flow: POST /orders with a PROMOTION product targeting this listing (see the Commerce & Plans collection, "Create order — Promotion").

item.name: Natural-language search
item.description: organizationId is optional and only meaningful when logged in (anonymous requests have no quota to pool). Leave {{organizationId}} empty for a personal search — it is never auto-selected from the caller's org memberships, even if they belong to an org with a bigger AI quota. Set it (and be an ACTIVE member of that org) to explicitly draw from that org's shared quota instead.

item.name: Send AI message (SSE stream)
item.description: organizationId is optional — leave {{organizationId}} empty to draw from the sender's own personal plan/free tier (the default; never auto-picked from their org memberships). Set it to explicitly pool this message against that org's shared AI quota; the caller must be an ACTIVE member or this returns 403 ORGANIZATION_ACCESS_DENIED.

item.name: Generate listing draft
item.description: organizationId is optional and rarely needs setting explicitly here: if propertyId refers to a property owned by an organization (not the caller personally), this draft's AI quota is automatically drawn from that org's plan — no organizationId needed. Set {{organizationId}} only to override that with a different org. With no propertyId at all, this always draws from the caller's personal plan.

item.name: Create organization
item.description: The creator is auto-added as OWNER, and the org is also granted a real, admin-editable Free plan row (same as an individual gets on registration).

item.name: My organizations
item.description: Scoped to the caller's own memberships only — for a platform-wide listing (any org, any status), see Admin — Organizations / List organizations. Filters: search, name, type, slug, phone, email, gstNumber, reraNumber, status, role.

item.name: Organization details
item.description: Public/optional-auth — works with or without a bearer token. 404s a PENDING or SUSPENDED organization unless the caller is one of its active members (admins are not exempt — see Admin — Organizations / Organization detail for the admin-safe equivalent).

item.name: Update organization
item.description: Requires the caller to be an active OWNER or ADMIN of the org. Only send the fields you want to change.

item.name: List members
item.description: Requires the caller to already be an active member of the org (any role) — this is what 403s a non-member admin, see Admin — Organizations / Organization detail for the workaround.

item.name: Add member (invite by email)
item.description: Invite-by-email only — there is no explicit-userId variant. Requires the caller to be an active OWNER or ADMIN of the org. If {{memberEmail}} already belongs to an existing user, that account is added as-is (name untouched) — otherwise a new, unverified account is created (email_verified_at stays null until proven via Auth — Member User below). Grants no platform role. role only accepts ADMIN or MEMBER — there is no way to grant OWNER here. Adding a genuinely new member is checked against the org's plan team-member limit — returns 403 PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED once at the plan's teamMembers cap (ACTIVE + INVITED both count). A brand-new org's FREE plan defaults to teamMembers: 1 (DEFAULT_FREE_TEAM_MEMBERS), and the OWNER already occupies that one seat — so this very first invite can 403 immediately on a fresh org. Confirmed live: this needs a real commerce.plan_subscriptions row for the org with a higher teamMembers to get past it (see the Zameens — Commerce & Payments collection's Admin — plan catalog / checkout flow for the real purchase path — there's no dev seed script for this yet). Run this BEFORE Auth — Member User.

item.name: Accept membership (as member user)
item.description: Run as the invited user, not the org owner — uses {{memberAccessToken}} (from Auth — Member User), not the collection default {{accessToken}}. The only path that moves a membership from INVITED to ACTIVE.

item.name: Remove member
item.description: Requires the caller to be an active OWNER or ADMIN of the org (and OWNER specifically to remove another OWNER). Blocks with 400 LAST_OWNER if the target is the org's only active owner. For an admin override that bypasses the OWNER/ADMIN requirement (and can also reactivate a REMOVED member), see Admin — Members / Update member status.

request.description: Each valid call creates an enquiry. UI must disable duplicate submission while this request is in flight. Any earlier unlinked, non-cancelled site visit for the buyer and listing is linked to this enquiry and changes its status to SITE_VISIT.

Links to the buyer's current active enquiry for this listing when one exists and changes it to SITE_VISIT atomically. Otherwise the visit remains unlinked until a later enquiry is created. It never creates a hidden enquiry. Repeating the same preferredDate + preferredTimeSlot while a non-cancelled visit already holds that slot fails with 409 SITE_VISIT_DUPLICATE, whose error.details carries the existing visitId.

item.name: List plans
item.description:
This is the pricing page's data source and the only place a client should read plan prices/limits from.

- Each plan returns `productId` — this, not the plan's own `id`, is what POST /orders needs.
- `aiMonthlyQuota` (integer, or null = unlimited) is the live source of truth for the AI Property Assistant's monthly question limit on that plan — don't hardcode this in the frontend.

item.name: List services
item.description:
Each service returns `productId` — required for POST /orders when purchasing it. The service's own `id` is only used for POST /service-requests, never for ordering.

Note: there is currently no public endpoint to discover PROMOTION products (their productId/price) — confirm with backend how a listing-boost screen should source that catalog before building it.

item.name: (Service purchase only) Create service request first
item.description: Only needed before purchasing a SERVICE product. Response is a ServiceRequest with `status: "REQUESTED"` and `orderId: null` — keep its `id`, it becomes `targetId` on the order below. Skip this step entirely for plans and promotions.

item.name: Create order — Plan
item.description:
For a plan, send only productId/quantity — no targetType/targetId (a PLAN item with a target is rejected with 400 INVALID_TARGET).

Response is the Order: `id`, `orderNumber`, `status: "CREATED"`, `items[]`, `subtotalMinor`, `taxMinor`, `totalMinor`, `currency`, `createdAt`, `paidAt`. The server always computes the price from the product row — nothing about price is client-controlled. Copy `id` → `orderId`. For the Pro plan above, expect `totalMinor: 49900`.

item.name: Create order — Promotion (boost a listing)
item.description:
`targetType` must be the literal string "LISTING" — anything else is rejected with 400. `targetId` must be a listing the logged-in user (or their organization) owns, or the order is rejected with 409 TARGET_NOT_OWNED. Only ever offer this action from the seller's own listing management screen.

Before sending the seller down this paid checkout path, try the free alternative first: POST /listings/{listingId}/feature (see the Dev 1 collection, Listings and moderation) draws from the plan's included monthly featuredListingsPerMonth allowance with no payment at all, and only falls back to 403 PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED (`checkoutRequired: true`) once that allowance is exhausted — that's the signal to offer this paid flow instead.

item.name: Create order — Paid service
item.description: `targetType` must be the literal string "SERVICE_REQUEST". `targetId` is the ServiceRequest id from the step above — it must belong to the current user and still be unpaid (`status: REQUESTED`, `orderId: null`), or this is rejected with 409 SERVICE_REQUEST_NOT_PAYABLE.

item.name: Create payment — returns a redirect URL, not a checkout payload
item.description:
`provider` defaults to "RAZORPAY" if omitted; it's the only provider actually implemented. Requires the order to belong to the caller and be CREATED or PAYMENT_PENDING (409 ORDER_ALREADY_PAID / ORDER_NOT_PAYABLE otherwise).

Response is only `{ paymentId, provider, redirectUrl }` — there is no `checkoutPayload`/`providerPublicKey`, no Razorpay key, SDK, or signature on the client. `redirectUrl` is a Razorpay-hosted Payment Link.

Frontend contract:
1. Do NOT load Razorpay Checkout.js or open a modal/iframe.
2. Do a full-page navigation: `window.location.href = redirectUrl`.
3. There is no POST /payments/verify endpoint — it does not exist; do not call it.
4. `returnUrl` is not an accepted field on this request — the redirect target is fixed server-side via COMMERCE_RETURN_BASE_URL.

Calling this again for the same order (e.g. the customer went back and retried) is safe — the previous Payment Link attempt is invalidated server-side and a fresh one is issued. Copy `paymentId` → `paymentId`.

item.name: GET order — poll this after redirect, don't trust the URL alone
item.description:
After the customer lands back on your `/payments/result?orderId=...&status=...` page, use this to confirm `status: "PAID"` rather than trusting the `status` query param alone for anything business-critical (e.g. don't unlock a feature purely because the URL said success — the query param can only drive which screen to show).

`/payments/result` status handling (docs/razorpay-client-integration-guide.md Section 5):
- `success` — captured, entitlement applied. Show success.
- `pending` — signature/lookup was fine but capture hasn't finished synchronously; poll this endpoint every few seconds (give up after ~30s) until `status: "PAID"`.
- `invalid` — signature didn't verify or the reference is unknown. Treat as failed, offer to retry.
- anything else (`cancelled`, `expired`, ...) — Razorpay's own status passed through as-is. Treat as not-paid, offer to retry via POST /payments/{orderId}/create again.

**`latestPaymentStatus` (new field, sits alongside `status`)** is the most recent payment attempt's own status (`CREATED`, `FAILED`, `CAPTURED`, ...). `status` alone cannot tell "still waiting on the current attempt" apart from "the last attempt failed, please retry" — both leave `status: "PAYMENT_PENDING"` on purpose, so a retry (POST /payments/{orderId}/create again) can reuse the same order instead of the order dead-ending. Check `latestPaymentStatus === "FAILED"` to show a retry prompt immediately on the result page instead of polling for up to 30s first.

item.name: Download invoice (PDF) — only once status is PAID
item.description:
Returns the tax invoice as a PDF (`Content-Type: application/pdf`, `Content-Disposition: attachment`), not JSON. 409 `INVOICE_NOT_AVAILABLE` if the order has never been captured — an invoice number is only assigned at payment-capture time, so there's nothing to generate before then. 404 `ORDER_NOT_FOUND` if the order doesn't belong to the caller (same owner-or-404 rule as GET order above).

GST breakdown (CGST+SGST vs IGST) is a display-only split of the already GST-inclusive plan/product price — it never changes `order.totalMinor` or what was actually charged.

item.name: GET my orders
item.description: Auth'd, paginated (`page`, `limit`), optional `status` filter (CREATED, PAYMENT_PENDING, PAID, FAILED, CANCELLED, REFUNDED — the validation layer accepts all six, but in practice no code path currently ever sets an order's own `status` to FAILED/CANCELLED/REFUNDED; a declined/expired payment attempt only ever shows up as that order's `latestPaymentStatus`, per the note above, while `status` stays PAYMENT_PENDING so the same order remains retryable).

item.name: GET my current plan
item.description:
Answers "what plan am I on and when does it end?" — a billing-status indicator (did I actually purchase something, and is it currently active), distinct from GET /me/subscription below (what effectively applies to me right now, features + limits + usage in one response). Use this one for a "my billing/plan" screen; use /me/subscription for anything that needs to show remaining quota/limits.

Response when the user has an active personal plan:
```json
{
  "hasActivePlan": true,
  "plan": { "id": "...", "productId": "...", "code": "PLAN_PRO_MONTHLY", "name": "Pro", ... },
  "status": "ACTIVE",
  "startsAt": "2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z",
  "endsAt": "2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z"
}
```
When there's no active plan (never purchased one, or it already lapsed): `{ "hasActivePlan": false, "plan": null, "status": null, "startsAt": null, "endsAt": null }` — deliberately still `false`/`null` even for an owner who's effectively on the Free plan by default; this endpoint only ever reports a REAL purchase/grant row, never the ambient Free-tier fallback.

There is no background sweep and no notification behind this — the query filters on `endsAt` lazily at read time, so a lapsed plan just stops being returned. The client is expected to read `endsAt` and decide for itself when to show "expiring soon"/"expired" messaging.

Organization-scoped plans are not returned here (personal plans only) — there is no equivalent "my org's plan" endpoint yet.

item.name: GET my full entitlement view (plan + limits + usage)
item.description:
The single response meant to power every UI surface that needs to show plan/usage together — My Zameens, the subscription/pricing page, upgrade banners, usage bars. Always returns a plan (never `null`/`hasActivePlan: false` like GET /plans/me above): if the caller has no real active purchase, this falls back to the live, admin-editable Free plan — not a hardcoded default, so an admin changing Free-tier limits via Admin: update plan is reflected here immediately, even for an owner who purchased something once and let it lapse.

```json
{
  "plan": { "code": "PLAN_PRO_MONTHLY", "name": "Pro", "monthlyPrice": 499 },
  "status": "ACTIVE",
  "currentPeriodStart": "2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z",
  "currentPeriodEnd": "2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z",
  "features": { "featuredListingsPerMonth": 2, "...": "..." },
  "limits": {
    "activeListings": { "used": 3, "limit": 10, "remaining": 7 },
    "imagesPerProperty": { "limit": 20 },
    "videosPerProperty": { "limit": 1 },
    "featuredListings": { "used": 0, "limit": 2, "remaining": 2 },
    "aiQueries": { "used": 4, "limit": null }
  }
}
```
`limit: null` on any block means unlimited (no `remaining` key in that case). This is personal-only, same as GET /plans/me — there is no organization-scoped equivalent yet.

item.name: Reference only — never called by the client directly
Payment callback (Razorpay redirects the BROWSER here)
item.description:
The frontend never fetches this with XHR/fetch — Razorpay's hosted Payment Link page redirects the customer's browser here after payment, and this endpoint itself responds with an HTTP 302 onward to `{COMMERCE_RETURN_BASE_URL}/payments/result?orderId=...&status=...`.

With a real (valid) signature and `razorpay_payment_link_status=paid`, the handler additionally calls Razorpay's GET /payments/{id} to confirm the payment's amount, currency, and captured status match the recorded payment before marking anything PAID — a mismatch or lookup failure redirects with `status=pending` instead (the webhook remains authoritative and will resolve it independently).

item.name: Payment webhook (server-to-server, Razorpay → our server)
item.description:
No UI relevance — included only so backend/QA can exercise the capture → entitlement path locally without a live Razorpay payment. The signature check rejects a fake header unless you compute a real HMAC-SHA256 of the exact raw body with your local RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET (see .env).

`payload.payment.entity.amount`, `.currency`, and `.status` must match the payment record exactly (amount in paise, currency case-insensitive, status literally "captured") — the handler now verifies all three against the stored payment before capturing, rejecting a mismatch with 409 PAYMENT_MISMATCH instead of silently marking the order paid. Set `amount` to the order's `totalMinor` and `status` to `"captured"` or this request will fail validation.

Duplicate delivery of the same event id is a safe no-op (`{ received: true, duplicate: true }`), in either arrival order relative to the callback above.

{
  "organizationId": "{{organizationId}}",
  "reraNumber": "RERA123456",
  "experienceYears": 5,
  "locationIds": ["{{locationId}}"],
  "about": "Experienced land broker covering the western suburbs."

request.description: organizationId is optional, but if set the caller must be an ACTIVE member of that organization (run Create organization first, which auto-adds the creator as OWNER) or the request fails with 403 ORGANIZATION_MEMBERSHIP_REQUIRED.

Response includes media (full array, each item with a signed url/thumbnailUrl) and documents (full array, each item with a signed downloadUrl) for the listing's property, same signing behavior as the public /listings/{listingId}/detail endpoint. Also includes location (location, pincode, addressLine, landmark, formattedAddress, latitude, longitude, locationPrecision, showExactLocation), or null if the property has no location saved yet — unlike the public endpoint, latitude/longitude are always exact here regardless of showExactLocation.
Removes one photo from the listing's property (e.g. inappropriate content). Audits the removal and notifies the seller with the given reason, or a default message if omitted.

item.name: Admin — approve and publish listing
item.description: Now also re-checks the seller's (or their organization's) active-listing plan limit at approval time, not just at submit time — a seller can submit several listings while under the limit and have several approved back-to-back, so this closes that gap. Returns 403 PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED (same nested `error.details.{feature,used,limit,upgradeRequired}` shape as everywhere else) if approving this one would push the owner over their plan's listingLimit, even though it was validly submitted while under the limit at the time.

request.description: Downloads a blank CSV template (correct headers/columns) for bulk listing import.
Multipart upload of a filled-in CSV (field name `file`). .csv only, max 10MB — rejects with INVALID_FILE_TYPE or FILE_TOO_LARGE otherwise.

item.name: Admin: update plan (change AI quota)
item.description: Changing aiMonthlyQuota only affects future usage windows — it never retroactively alters a customer's already-counted usage this month. Note: `code` cannot be changed once the plan has any orders against it (409 PLAN_CODE_LOCKED).

item.name: Admin: deactivate plan
item.description: Deactivated plans drop out of GET /plans and cannot be ordered, but do not affect anyone who already purchased them.

request.description: Platform-wide listing, not scoped to the caller's own memberships (unlike GET /organizations/me) — so PENDING and SUSPENDED organizations are visible here too, which the member-gated public GET /organizations/{organizationId} would otherwise 404 for a non-member admin. Filters: search, name, type, slug, phone, email, gstNumber, reraNumber, status.

Same as the public GET /organizations/{organizationId} but bypasses its active-membership visibility gate, so a PENDING or SUSPENDED organization can be reviewed before/without approving it. Also inlines a `members` array (user, role, status, joinedAt for each) — the public detail response never includes this, and the dedicated GET /organizations/{organizationId}/members endpoint would 403 an admin who isn't themselves a member.
PENDING → ACTIVE. Fails with 409 INVALID_TRANSITION if the organization isn't currently PENDING.

PENDING or ACTIVE → SUSPENDED (there's no separate REJECTED status, so this doubles as rejecting a pending organization). reason is required. Fails with 409 INVALID_TRANSITION if the organization is already SUSPENDED.
SUSPENDED → ACTIVE. Fails with 409 INVALID_TRANSITION if the organization isn't currently SUSPENDED.

Admin-only: sets an organization member's status directly to ACTIVE, INVITED, or REMOVED, bypassing the org's own OWNER/ADMIN requirement (unlike the self-service Remove member request under Organizations). Unlike Remove member, this can also reactivate a REMOVED member straight to ACTIVE/INVITED with no fresh invite-accept cycle and no team-member seat-limit re-check — a deliberate admin override. Still blocks 400 LAST_OWNER if the target is the org's only active OWNER and the new status isn't ACTIVE. There's no SUSPENDED status distinct from REMOVED without a schema migration.
